# Lab 4.14: Global Queries

## What We Are Going to Do
Turn on global queries (Preview) and run one query that joins a US dataset with a dataset in another region.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create a dataset in another region.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq --location=asia-south1 mk --dataset $PROJECT_ID:lab04_mumbai
bq --location=asia-south1 query --use_legacy_sql=false \
'CREATE TABLE lab04_mumbai.targets AS
 SELECT "India" AS country, 5000 AS target_orders UNION ALL SELECT "Japan", 3000'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Enable global queries.** Needs BigQuery Admin. Run in the console. Replace `YOUR_PROJECT`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">ALTER PROJECT `YOUR_PROJECT`
SET OPTIONS (`region-us.enable_global_queries_execution` = TRUE);

ALTER PROJECT `YOUR_PROJECT`
SET OPTIONS (`region-asia-south1.enable_global_queries_data_access` = TRUE);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Run the two statements separately. They can take a few minutes to apply.

3. **[SQL] Run the cross-region join.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT u.country, COUNT(*) AS orders, ANY_VALUE(t.target_orders) AS target
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` o
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` u ON o.user_id = u.id
JOIN lab04_mumbai.targets t ON t.country = u.country
GROUP BY u.country;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   In **Query settings**, set the processing location to **US**. The `asia-south1` data is copied to the US for this query.

4. **[Console] Look at the job.** In **Job information**, the job is a global query with child jobs in `asia-south1`.

5. **[SQL] Turn it off again.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">ALTER PROJECT `YOUR_PROJECT`
SET OPTIONS (`region-us.enable_global_queries_execution` = FALSE,
             `region-asia-south1.enable_global_queries_data_access` = FALSE);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Default | Global queries are off |
| Permission | `bigquery.jobs.createGlobalQuery` (BigQuery Admin) |
| Join | US and Mumbai data in one query |
| Cost | Compute in both regions, plus data transfer; no query cache |
